page: Google Cloud Platform a3-edgegpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server configured with eight NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs providing a total of 637 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by Intel Xeon 8481C processors on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 208 vCPUs across 104 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. It features 1872 GB of system memory, translating to 9.0 GB per core, and includes 6432 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 13661.0 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 431.78 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations and Redis SET throughput also place in the top 10%, with Redis achieving 177.5 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Passmark memory scores falling in the middle 50% tier.

Given the massive GPU and memory resources, this server is designed for heavy parallel workloads such as large language model training, high-performance computing, and complex database operations. LLM text generation benchmarks show 29.51 tokens per second for a medium 7B model and 3.7 tokens per second for a large 70B model. The integration of high-density GPU accelerators and local NVMe storage provides high resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for massive scale-out AI and data science workloads despite the high baseline hardware profile.
description: Google Cloud Platform a3-edgegpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server designed for high-demand parallel computing and machine learning workloads. It features eight NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs with 637 GB of total VRAM, paired with 208 vCPUs from Intel Xeon 8481C processors and 1872 GB of system memory. Storage is supported by 6432 GB of local NVMe SSDs. In benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and high database throughput, though single-core CPU and memory latency scores remain in the average tier. Advanced instruction sets like Intel AMX and AVX-512 are fully supported. This configuration is highly suited for large-scale AI model training, LLM inference, high-performance computing, and intensive database operations.
